A_target.statement:
Let $\gamma$ be a unit-speed [[Definition:Curve|curve]] in $\R^3$ with [[Definition:Curvature|curvature]] $\kappa > 0$.
Let $T = \gamma'$, $N = T' / \kappa$ and $B = T \times N$.
Then there is a function $\tau$, the [[Definition:Torsion of Curve|torsion]], with:
:$T' = \kappa N, \quad N' = -\kappa T + \tau B, \quad B' = -\tau N$

B_source.statement:
Let $\gamma$ be a unit-speed plane curve with unit tangent $T$, unit normal $N$ and signed curvature $\kappa$.
Then:
:$T' = \kappa N, \quad N' = -\kappa T$

object_map.reformulation: Express the derivative of a moving orthonormal frame by a skew-symmetric coefficient matrix; in three dimensions it has one new entry.

validity_conditions: kappa > 0 is needed to define N.
Differentiating the orthonormality relations forces the coefficient matrix to be skew-symmetric.
proof_plan:
In the plane, $\tuple {T, N}$ is an orthonormal frame, and differentiating $\innerprod {e_i} {e_j} = \delta_{i j}$ shows that $e_i' = \sum_j a_{i j} e_j$ with $\paren {a_{i j} }$ skew-symmetric.
The only entry is $a_{12} = \kappa$.
In $\R^3$, $\tuple {T, N, B}$ is a positively oriented orthonormal frame, and the same computation gives a $3 \times 3$ skew-symmetric matrix.
Its entries are $\innerprod {T'} N = \kappa$, $\innerprod {T'} B = 0$ as $T'$ is parallel to $N$, and $\tau = \innerprod {N'} B$.
